proposals.idea: A foreground point mass at low Galactic latitude is lensing a steady red background star, producing the smooth brightening attributed to a young Type Ia. The lens adds no light of its own but achromatically amplifies the source above its constant baseline.
proposals.name: Unseen microlens magnification
proposals.predicts: It predicts a time-symmetric, colour-constant rise and fall that returns to the pre-event baseline, unlike a Type Ia's asymmetric radioactive decline and evolving colour.

proposals.idea: An unseen compact object in the Galactic plane is microlensing a faint background star, producing the accelerating rise that supernova templates severely underpredict. The faint pre-rise detections are blended baseline light, whose relative contribution declines as magnification increases, explaining the apparent bluing.
proposals.name: Galactic microlensing surge
proposals.predicts: The transient will peak soon and then decline symmetrically with the same t0, u0, and tE in g and r, approaching a constant source colour at high magnification and returning to its pre-event baseline rather than following supernova colour evolution and a radioactive tail.

proposals.idea: In this crowded low-latitude ZTF field a flawed reference template leaves a constant host or nearby-star residual, while a slowly drifting photometric zero point adds a linear flux ramp in each band. Together they mimic an accelerating supernova rise that the Ia and Ibc templates are too slow to match, without any real point-source explosion.
proposals.name: Drifting calibration subtraction ramp
proposals.predicts: It predicts the flux keeps increasing linearly in microjansky with roughly constant g-r colour and an extended or offset subtraction residual in the stamps, with no supernova peak, cooling reddening, or subsequent decline.
